translations.text: A eulogy delivered by our holy father Flavian, bishop of the city of Ephesus, which he delivered in honor of Saint
Demetrius, archbishop of Alexandria, on the day of his honored commemoration, the twenty-eighth of the month of Thoth.
He also spoke about the miracles that God performed through him.
He also spoke in this same encomium about the holy martyr and virgin, Apa Peter, the archbishop of this same city, Alexandria.
And about the holy woman martyr from the city of Antioch and her two sons, Philopator and Eutropius.
He also spoke about the consolation of the soul and about the saying written in Jeremiah the prophet: “On that day I will raise up a righteous Branch in the house of David.”
In the peace of God. Amen.

The occasion now moves me to set in motion the instrument of my feeble tongue and my weak mouth, so that I too may say with David, the psalmist and singer of praises to God: “You visited the earth and made it drunk; you greatly enriched it.”
The river of God is full of water.
You prepared their food, for this is truly our provision.
He visited the earth and made it drunk; he greatly enriched it.
If earthly wine brings people joy, although when they drink too much of it they fall down, and it causes illness,
then how great are the gladness and joy of those who have drunk from the spring of living water, Christ!
If the earth rejoices when rain from heaven comes upon it, then how great are the gladness and joy of people when the spiritual rainwater comes upon the spiritual field!
Visible rain produces visible, physical fruit.
When the spiritual rain came upon the earth, people bore spiritual fruit.
What, then, are those fruits?
Listen, and I will tell you.
Only do not doubt or grumble.
Only one church has closed.
I am speaking of the synagogue of the Jews.
I am not, however, calling this a spiritual church. For this very reason, indeed, they closed it,
through him who rose from the dead and sat at the right hand of his Father, who became human at his command.
Thousands upon thousands and tens of thousands upon tens of thousands have been opened to us through his holy blood, which was poured out for us.
The fruits I mentioned earlier are these: self-control, purity, virginity, mercy, peace, hope, generosity, obedience, and the things that follow these.
These are what the spiritual field brought forth through the spiritual rain that came upon it.
Now is the time for me to say, with the prophet and lawgiver Moses, “Let us sing to the Lord, for he has been glorified in glory.”
If those people marveled when they saw their enemies dying in the sea, then why should I not marvel when I see the one who died for us and rose again to humble the proud?
Now, then, let me set in motion the instrument of my tongue and speak a few words of honor for this saint, in whose holy name we are gathered.
He is a father who loves his children.
He is a shepherd who tends his flock well, clothed in the two virtues: virginity and honorable marriage.
But perhaps someone will say to me, “A person cannot be a virgin after taking a wife.”
Let that person listen. I will give him proof from the holy Scriptures.
Let me too say, with our Savior, that there are some who have made themselves eunuchs for the sake of the kingdom of heaven.
For the eunuchs who are born from their mother’s womb as eunuchs have only the name.
But the eunuch who makes himself a eunuch—who can speak of his courage?
For if David had struck down Goliath while wearing military equipment, they would not have praised him so greatly.
But when he struck him down without weapons or a belt, like [?] all those who died, and the songs of victory, which are praises [?].
Likewise, if a person who was born a eunuch struggles, they will not count it as courage on his part as they would for someone who struggles while possessing his bodily members.
For David struck down the lion and the bear once or twice, or even three times.
But Demetrius the archbishop struck down sensual pleasures every day.
Fighting wild beasts is not an act of courage like fighting the passions.
If wild beasts devour a person, they do not find him again for him to fight them.
But sensual pleasure never stops striking every day at the person who gives it room within himself, until it destroys him, as it grows within him.
The wise, self-controlled people know this, and that is why they flee to the desert.
Nevertheless, let us now return our discussion to this holy man and tell you about his virtues and his acts of courage.
Now the holy Demetrius was one of the eminent presbyters renowned in the city of Alexandria.
For after Saint Julian, archbishop of Alexandria, died, the throne of Alexandria remained for many days
vacant, without a bishop. No one sat on the archiepiscopal throne, because it was the time of the lawless kings
and idol worshipers. A great persecution was being waged against the church, and the people were like sheep without a shepherd.
Then, by the will of God and the vote of all the people, they took hold of a new Joseph.
I mean Saint Demetrius. They seated him on the throne of Saint Mark the Evangelist.
But perhaps you will say to me, you who are listening, “Granted that you compare this saint to Joseph, you have not compared the wife of this holy and chaste man to that worthless woman
who envied Saint Joseph—I mean the Egyptian woman.”
No, no! May it never be! But forgive me, people who love Christ.
For if Joseph had slept with the Egyptian woman, it would have been a sin for him.
For what he would have done was sexual immorality. That is why he kept his body holy for God, who created him.
But if the holy Demetrius had slept with his wife, there would have been no sin for him: they had been joined to one another by God.
But you will certainly say, “He is a bishop; it was not [?] proper for him to marry.”
Do not speak that way, brother.
For indeed, the holy canons of the apostles say this: “If a man has a wife before becoming a bishop,
and afterward becomes a bishop, he must not send her away, but must remain with her.”
The holy apostle says, “Marriage is honorable in every respect, and the marriage bed is undefiled.”
It is the sexually immoral and adulterers whom God will judge.
This holy man, then, acted in accordance with what we have said.
When they appointed him to the episcopal throne, then, what sort of thing was this?
Do not give to him.
And he would say to him, “My son, go and turn away from whatever sin you are committing. After that, partake of the holy mysteries.”
So, when he continued steadfastly in this way, the whole city turned away from sins. But as [?] from sins.
Now, when someone sees another person committing a sin, he rebukes him, saying, “Stop doing this,
lest the archbishop shame you while all the people are watching you.” And that person becomes afraid and stops.
For this reason, many turned away and refrained from sinning.
Nevertheless, many troublemakers would say, “Does this man not have his wife with him, while he speaks these words in this way?”
And they were all offended, and there was grumbling about him, because since Saint Mark the evangelist, no one had sat on the archbishop’s throne unless he was a virgin.
But some of those who understood the Scriptures would say to those who spoke these words, “Marriage is honorable in conduct,
and the marriage bed is undefiled.
And God is the one who created it.
Why are you grumbling against the archbishop?”
Nevertheless, they could not persuade them. They said, “This is the twelfth
to sit on the archiepiscopal throne, and no one except this man alone has a wife.”
But God himself, the good one, who does not want his saints to remain hidden, wanted to reveal them and to receive glory through them,
just as he said in the Gospel: “People do not light a lamp and put it under a measuring basket. Rather, they put it on the lampstand so that it gives light to everyone in the house.”
And he revealed the matter to the archbishop while he was sleeping one night.
Then an angel of God appeared to him and said to him, “Demetrius, Demetrius, do not seek only your own good, but also the good of your neighbor.”
And again, remember what the Lord said in the Gospel: “The good shepherd lays down his life for his sheep.”

Saint Demetrius answered and said to the angel, “What is happening, my lord? Or what are you commanding me to do? Are you sending me to martyrdom? I am ready to pour out my blood for the name of my Lord Jesus Christ.”
The angel said to him, “Listen to me, Demetrius.
Christ became human because he loves us, and also to save his people.
Now then, is it right [?] for you to cause the people over whom God appointed you to stumble?”
The archbishop said to the angel, “My lord, tell me my sin so that I may turn away from it.”
The angel said to him, “Reveal to all the people the secret between you and your wife.”
Demetrius said, “I beg you, my lord, let me die before you. Not only must you not let this happen, but you must not let anyone know about it either.”
The angel said to him, “You yourself know, Demetrius, what is written: ‘The disobedient person will come to ruin.’
So rise early in the morning.
After you have dismissed the congregation, gather all the clergy and the devoted workers, and tell them the secret between you and your wife.”
When the angel had said these things to him, he disappeared from his sight.
When morning came, it was the day of holy Pentecost. The archbishop held a general worship assembly.
On that day, when he had explained the teaching to the people with his holy mouth.
Then, after receiving the holy mysteries and completing his liturgy,
The archbishop commanded the archdeacon not to let anyone among all the people leave, but to have them gather in the assembly hall, saying
this: “The archbishop commands you: ‘Do not let any of you go away, for I have something to tell you.
When they had sat down in the assembly hall, the archbishop ordered a large quantity of wood to be gathered. He had fire brought and set the wood alight.
The people were astonished and said, “What is this?”
Then the pope said, “Stand up, and let us pray.”
After they had prayed, they sat down.
The pope said to them, “I appeal to your love: let your servant, who is my wife, come forward and receive your blessing.”
They were astonished and said, “Our father, let everything you command be done.”
The archbishop called one of his servants and said to him, “Go and call the servant of these holy people, who is my wife.”
When the holy woman heard, she came into the midst of the brothers.
The archbishop rose while they all watched him. He stood on the burning coals, spread out his cloak, picked up burning coals with his hands, and put them into his cloak.
All the brothers sitting in the assembly hall were astonished that, despite the blaze of the coals, his cloak did not burn.
Then he said to his wife, “Spread out your cloak and your shawl.”
The holy man transferred the coals into her shawl. She too remained standing beside him in the midst of the fire, and neither she nor her shawl burned.
The archbishop said a second time, “Let us pray.” The burning coals were in her shawl, but it did not burn.
Listen, and marvel with me, my beloved ones.
For I have said that if a person makes himself a eunuch, he is more honored than someone born a eunuch.
That is precisely why these holy people did not burn: they had extinguished the flame of the fire of pleasure.
Now, so that we do not stray from the subject—
let us return and finish the story to the glory of God.
After they had prayed, they sat down.
The clergy said to the archbishop, “We ask Your Holiness to tell us what this demonstration you have performed means, for we are all astonished at what happened.”
He said to them, “Listen to me, and I will tell you. I did not do this to seek human praise.
For I am sixty years old today,
and the woman you see is the same age as I am.

Her father died while she was still little, and her father's brother, who is my father, brought her into our home. She was an only child, as I too was an only child, and we were raised together in the same place.
When I turned eighteen, my parents wanted to marry me to her.
First, because we were relatives of one another, and then also because of this world's vanity, so that no stranger would come among us and take any of our inheritance.
When they held our wedding according to what is proper among people, they instructed me to go in to her.
When we lay down, she said to me, “My brother, does a brother marry his sister?”
I said to her, “No.”
Then she said to me, “Why did they give us to one another? Am I not your sister?”
But I said to her, “If you listen to me, my sister, we will be in the place where we will never be separated from one another.”
“But if I marry you here, they will separate me from you and separate you from me through death.
If, on the other hand, we keep our bodies holy in purity, we will not pass one another by in the heavenly Jerusalem.”
When she heard these words from me, we made an agreement with one another to keep our bodies undefiled.
My parents, however, did not know about the matter.
Instead, they would tell the people in the bridal chamber to bring the evidence of the bride's virginity, as you know about the things people customarily do.
These people, in turn, would persuade our parents, saying, “They are young children.”
Through these words, our parents stopped questioning us.
When our parents died, we remained together as orphans.
As for these three children whom we have kept with us, it was God who placed them together.
And a single covering covers the two of us together, except at the time when a woman separates herself from a man.
And the Lord knows this, he who will judge the living and the dead.
And he knows the secrets of the heart: I do not know that she is a woman, nor does she herself know that I am a man, except only from one another's faces.
But we know nothing at all of the sexual union of the bed that belongs to this world.
When we lie down together, we see a creature like an eagle flying. It comes and spreads its covering over the bed of the two of us.
It covers me with its right wing.
And it covers her with its left wing.
At daylight each morning, it departs while we watch it.
And do not think that I am seeking human glory. No! Nor was it my wish
to tell you this, except that he who wishes to benefit everyone—God, who loves humanity—commanded me.’”
When he said these things, they fell at his feet, saying, “Truly, our father, you are honored above all creation.”
After this, he instructed his wife to withdraw to her own place.
He prayed for them too and dismissed them, so that each could go home in peace.
Were your hearts not stirred within you as you heard such great wonders? Did you not marvel at this saint,
who spent his whole life with his wife, abstaining from sexual relations with her?
Where now are those who commit sexual immorality even though they have wives, especially those who say, “We are Christians”?
Let them come now and be ashamed when they see their father Demetrius, the holy archbishop, saying, “We do not know each other except by appearance alone.”
O overseer of the contest and fighter against the passions, Saint Demetrius! O my father, was your heart not stirred within you when you saw your wife, who was so beautiful?
Did the softness of her plump body not cloud your thoughts, since you were a young boy, especially when you spoke with her and no one was near you?
“Has the evil archer not shot at you?” “Yes,” he said. “I too am a human being, clothed in flesh like everyone else.”
But listen, and I will tell you: whenever my heart is stirred within me toward passion,
I remember the covenants I made with Christ, so that I do not break them.
He too will disown me before his Father and his holy angels.
And whenever I remember the softness of her body,
I remember the ugliness of the bodies in the tombs and their stench.
we remain silent and do not speak improper words, because we fear the threat of the fire and the flame of Gehenna, which is in the underworld.
Those who are in it wish to open their mouths at all, but they cannot open them.
I remember, O assembly of those who love God, that I said at the beginning of the introduction that this holy man is more excellent than someone who strikes down a lion and a bear.
For one of the philosophers said, “Someone who strikes down a lion is not a mighty man,
and someone who strikes down a panther is not a powerful man.
But someone who dies untouched by the deceit of women is a mightier man.”
Joseph the patriarch was staying in the house of the Egyptian woman.
It is clear that that lawless woman was wicked and spoke with him every day until she found an opportunity against him.
But you, O holy Demetrius, are attacked every day through your thoughts.
I would have liked to spend more time speaking with you and recounting to you the virtues, miracles, and mighty deeds of this holy man.
But I know that his honor is in heaven, beside the one who became human for our sake through Mary the virgin.
Truly, you have completed the race.
You have kept the faith.
And you are interceding for us now in the place where you are.
I would indeed like to speak at length with you and tell you about the wonders that God performed through this holy man, Saint Demetrius, the holy archbishop.
But I know my own infirmity and the weakness of my humble words.
But let us turn to another subject and bring forward a man who possessed three virtues: virginity, the high priesthood, and martyrdom.
Who, then, is this? It is Saint Peter, the archbishop of Alexandria.
At that time, then, idolatry prevailed under the lawless emperor Diocletian.
He had ordered the churches everywhere to be demolished, and no one was conducting holy worship openly except in Alexandria alone, because the holy archbishop Peter was not angry at anyone.
Rather, he placed his trust in the one who said, “Do not fear those who will kill your body but have no power to kill your soul.”
For this reason he grew even stronger, and he used to tell the clergy, “Do not let apprehension about people separate you from Christ.”
There was a man in Antioch at that time whose name was Socrator.
He was a friend of Apater, who had gone to Egypt and become a martyr.
This Socrator had originally been a Christian and had received baptism.
But he renounced it.
He was a hypocrite who hated Christians intensely. He had a Christian wife named Martyria, who had borne him two sons.
He named the older one Philopator.
And the younger one Eutropius.
When the little children grew older, they reached the age for baptism.
And for them to be baptized according to Christian practice.
The woman spoke to her husband, saying, “I beg you, my brother, to come with me to the city of Alexandria so that we can have our children baptized, lest they die without receiving baptism and God
be angry with us because we neglected our children’s souls.”
But he said to her, “Be quiet, my sister. You know that persecution is taking place now.
The emperor might hear about it and threaten us.” He said this so that she would be afraid and would not have her children baptized.
When she realized that he would not agree to what she had planned, she got up, took her two sons by the hand, and went out to the sea.
She prayed in this way, saying, “Lord God Almighty, Father of my Lord Jesus Christ,
if you will make my path straight, then grant me an opportunity.”
While she was still praying, she looked and saw a ship sailing on the sea. The woman called to those aboard the ship, “Where are you going?”
They said to her, “We are going to the city of Alexandria.”
She said to them, “Can you take me aboard with you? I will pay you your fare.”
They said to her, “Yes, we will take you aboard.”
And in this way they took her aboard and set sail.
When they had gone twenty stadia, a great storm arose over the ship, so that everyone aboard was terrified.
That God-loving woman said, “God does not listen to sinners like me, but I will do what has come into my heart.”
She got up, stood, and prayed facing east, saying, “God, you who know all things before they happen,
You are the one who knows everyone’s heart, and you know my heart’s desire toward you.
For I do not want a husband, or clothing—it belongs to this world—or possessions like yours, or even your soul and my children.
Look, we are going to die in the sea.”
For the sake of your holy name, my Lord Jesus Christ, the Savior of my soul and my spirit, look down upon me and my two orphaned children, and have mercy on us.
When she had said this, she took a blade in her right hand. She drew the blade out and made the sign of the cross over it.
She pierced her right breast and brought three drops of blood out of it.
She marked the foreheads of her two children and their chests with the sign of the cross, in the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
and immersed them three times in the sea in the name of the Holy Trinity, saying, “In the name of the Holy Trinity, the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.”
After this she gathered them into her lap, saying, “I am going to die. Let me die with my children.”
But when God, the Master of all, saw her faith, he calmed the storm, and a great calm followed. Within three days they reached Alexandria.
With God’s help, they entered Alexandria on Friday in the fourth week
of Easter, during which they customarily baptize little children according to the tradition of the Egyptians.
The woman saw that the whole city was dressed in white, and she asked, “What is happening?”
They told her, “All the Christians who live in this city will baptize their children tomorrow.”
She replied, “Truly, the Lord has made my path straight.”
She approached a deacon and said to him, “My father, I want to meet the archbishop.”
He said to her, “What business do you have with the archbishop?”
She said to him, “I am a foreigner, and I want to have my children baptized.”
The deacon said to her, “Do you have no other business with the archbishop besides this?”
She said, “No.”
The deacon said to her, “If this is the only business for which you want to meet the archbishop, then sit down.
Look, tomorrow they will baptize the young children who are in this city. They will baptize your children along with them.”
When night came, the archbishop completed the holy service. Afterward he ordered them to bring the little children who had been prepared for baptism.
And while he was baptizing, they brought in the children of the woman from Antioch.
But God, who alone performs wonders, concealed the matter from the archbishop.
But when he took hold of the little children to baptize them, the baptismal font froze and became stone.
When the archbishop saw this, he was greatly astonished. He ordered them to be set aside.
He ordered the young children of the people of Alexandria to be brought in to him.
When he began to baptize them, the baptismal font became water again, as before.
Immediately he ordered the children of the woman from Antioch to be brought to him again.
When they were brought forward, the baptismal font turned to stone as before.
He ordered the little children to be set aside again.
He ordered the young children from Alexandria to be brought.
When they were brought in for him to baptize them, the baptismal font became water again, as before.
Then he ordered the children of the woman from Antioch to be brought in to him for the third time. Immediately the water in the baptismal font froze and became like stone.
Saint Peter, the archbishop, ordered the archdeacon to bring the woman from Antioch forward.
When they brought her to stand before him, the archbishop said to her, “Tell me what happened to you,
or what it was that you did. And where do they come from, in terms of their religion? Or [?] which city?”
The mother of the little children answered and said to the archbishop, “My parents and I are Christians, and I am from Antioch.”
The archbishop answered and said to her, "Tell me what you have done. For look, God has not accepted your children into repentance."
The woman said, "Listen to me with understanding, my lord and father.
For you know the sufferings that exist in the world, and now all the more in Antioch.
My children had grown older, and I had not found an opportunity to baptize them.
I said to their father, 'Get up. Let us go to the city of Alexandria, into the presence of Your Holiness, and baptize our children.'
He did not want to do this. Instead, he threatened to bring other dangers upon me.
So I got up, took my two children by the hand, and went out to the sea. I found a ship bound for Alexandria.
I boarded it with my children.
When we reached the middle of the sea, the ship was endangered by great storms, so that it was about to sink.
I took hold of my two children, intending to throw myself into the sea and die with them.
But a thought came into my heart, and I took a knife in my hand.
I pricked my right finger and drew three drops of blood from it.
I marked their foreheads and their chests with the seal, saying, 'In the name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit.'
And I immersed them in the sea in the name of the Holy Trinity.
Surely it was for this reason, my lord and father, that the Lord preserved my life and those of my children."
But I know of nothing else I have done apart from this alone.
The archbishop said to the woman, “Take courage, my daughter. The Lord is with you. What you did was good.
And the one you approached when you pierced your right thumb and put its blood on your children’s foreheads—the one whose side was pierced with a spear on the cross—
he is the one who sealed your children with his own hands. And when you immersed them in the sea, it was our Lord who immersed them with his hands.”
Immediately the archbishop left them without baptizing them; he only said the prayer over her and her children.
And he delivered this exhortation that day, revealing God’s love for humanity and his compassion.
He gave the children a little of the holy mysteries and kept them with him until the celebration of holy Easter was concluded.
Afterward he sent her and her children back to her city in peace.
When her husband saw that she had returned to him, he went to Diocletian, the lawless emperor, who was more wicked than anyone on earth.
He said to him, “You know that my wife committed sexual immorality here. I did not tolerate her.
When she saw that I would not tolerate her, she got up and went to Alexandria, to that contemptible Peter.
She committed sexual immorality with them in baptism, and she introduced my children to their filthy mysteries.
Look, many days have passed since she went away, and now she has returned here. What do you want me to do, my lord the emperor?”
The king said to him, “Socrator, who is doing these things in Alexandria?”
He said, “Peter, the one they call archbishop?”
When the king heard, he threw her out, because he was angry with him, Saint Peter,
ever since he had read his discourse about the idols, which he delivered against them.
He sent a tribune and soldiers to Alexandria to behead Saint Peter.
He ordered that Zocrator’s wife be brought with her two children.
When they brought her, he said to her, “Woman, why did you leave your husband and go and commit sexual immorality with the Christians?”
The martyr Martyria answered with a single statement: “Christians do not commit sexual immorality, nor do they worship idols.
Now do whatever you want to me.
But I will not listen to a word from your mouth.”
The emperor said to her, “Tell me what happened there.”
But she did not answer him at all.
The king became angry and ordered them to bind her hands and feet [?] behind her,
place her two children on top of her, and burn them alive together, all at once.
She turned her face toward the east and offered her prayer.
You have seen, my beloved, that God has someone who does his will at every moment.
He said, “She turned her face toward the east and immediately gave up her spirit, because her holy heart was always looking toward the east.”
For the trees of paradise were created in the regions of the east, and the devil brought Adam out of it through envy.
God himself, who became human, was also envied by the devil.
He will bring us back to him again through his holy blood, which was poured out for us.
The true dawn that rose from the house of David.
For a star will rise in Jacob. This is the star that the Magi saw in the east when they brought their gifts to Christ. This had been foretold through the prophet.
But we know that the dawn [?], we who are in darkness and the shadow of death.
I think, O Christ-loving assembly, that we have found the man.
your love, according to the measure of our discipleship. For we are disciples of the great true teacher, our Lord, our Savior.
Through him, glory be to the Father, together with him and the Holy Spirit, who gives life and is of the same essence, now and always and forever. Amen.
